html:
Konnaack is the name on the map for a small area on the lower Columbia River, on the Oregon side between today's Clatskanie and Rainier. Little reliable information about the name is available. It likely refers to a Chinookan village or band of this stretch of the river.

The lower Columbia was the land of Chinookan peoples such as the Kathlamet and Clatsop. They lived in cedar plank houses, fished for salmon and sturgeon, and controlled a busy river trade. Fever epidemics in the early 1830s killed most of the people of the lower river, and survivors later joined the reservations of Grand Ronde and others.
